01 · The brand

Specialists in small patients

Pediatric Ear, Nose & Throat Specialists is a physician group that treats only children, from newborns through teens, across six Tampa Bay offices. Parents arrive worried, often late at night, often on a phone. Everything the brand does should lower the temperature in the room.

Promise

Expert care scaled to the child in front of us. The tagline says it plainly: Insist on the Right Size Care.

Audience

Parents and caregivers in Hillsborough, Pinellas, Pasco and Sarasota counties, plus the pediatricians who refer them. Kids are the patients; parents are the readers.

Personality

Warm, calm, competent, a little playful. Think of a great pediatric nurse: unhurried, clear, and kind without being cutesy.

Why the colors softened

The original logo used primary red, yellow and blue at full strength. That reads as energetic and toy-like, which suits a children's brand but fights the calm a worried parent needs. The Muted palette keeps the same three hues and the same three animals, lowers the saturation, and lets the brand feel like a well-run practice that happens to be for kids. A pale Sage Tint joins as the fifth core color, for confirmations and calm backgrounds. Nothing about the mark's shape changed, so existing signage and recognition carry over.

02 · Logo

The primary lockup

The logo is a single unit: the bunny, the elephant, the giraffe and the two-line wordmark. The elephant sits behind the wordmark on purpose and should never be separated from it in the full lockup.

Reversed. On Denim, Charcoal or photography, the wordmark becomes white and the animals keep their colors.

One-color Charcoal. For fax headers, embroidery, engraving, and any single-ink print.

One-color white. For Charcoal or photo grounds where the full-color version would lose the Denim giraffe.

On tints. Full color works on any of the three tints and on Cloud. Do not place it on Coral, Butter or Denim at full strength.

Clear space and minimum size

Keep a margin equal to the height of the capital P in "Pediatric" on all four sides. Nothing enters that zone: no text, rules, photos or page edges.

CLEAR SPACE = CAP HEIGHT OF "P"
Print minimum · 1.75 in wide
Screen minimum · 140 px wide

Below these sizes the bunny's eye and the giraffe's horns fill in. For favicons, app icons and social avatars use a single animal from chapter 03, never the full lockup.

What not to do

03 · The three friends

Bunny, Elephant, Giraffe

Each animal carries one of the three brand colors and loosely maps to the practice's three specialties. They may appear alone as icons, avatars and illustration, always in their own color.

Bunny · Ear

Always Coral. The go-to avatar and favicon; its silhouette holds up smallest. Faces right.

Elephant · Nose

Always Butter. Because the elephant interlocks with the wordmark, cut the standalone mark from the vector master only. Never trace it from a raster.

Giraffe · Throat

Always Denim. The tallest mark; use it for vertical spaces like signage edges and story templates.

Rules for the animals

  • Each animal keeps its own color. A Denim bunny or a Coral giraffe is a misuse.
  • Animals may sit on their own tint, on Cloud, on white, or reversed in white on their own full-strength color.
  • They are silhouettes, not characters. No added faces, clothing, expressions or speech bubbles.
  • Use one at a time as an icon. Use all three together only in the logo or as a decorative row at the foot of a page.
  • Keep them flat. No 3D, bevels or textures.
04 · Color

Three soft hues, one quiet ground

Coral, Butter and Denim do the color work, Charcoal carries the words, and Sage Tint is the calm fifth for confirmations and gentle backgrounds. Everything else is near-neutral so the hues stay special. Values below are the master values; use HEX for screen, CMYK as a starting point for print and match to a press proof.

Proportion

Most of any layout is white, Cloud and a tint. Denim leads the hues; Coral is the action color; Butter is the smallest and brightest, used like a highlighter; Sage Tint is a quiet field for confirmations.

White & Cloud 40%Tints 18%Sage Tint 7%Denim 17%Coral 9%Butter 4%Charcoal 5%

Accessibility

WCAG 2.1 contrast ratios on the grounds you will actually use. "Large" means 18 pt regular or 14 pt bold and above, or UI icons and borders.

Text colorOn whiteOn CloudOn tints (incl. Sage Tint)Use for text
Charcoal8.9 : 18.1 : 17.1 – 7.9 : 1AAA any size, any ground
Denim3.9 : 13.6 : 13.2 : 1Large headings & icons only
Coral3.2 : 12.9 : 12.6 : 1Large headings only on white
Butter1.6 : 11.5 : 11.5 : 1Never a text color

Reversed and on color: white on Denim 3.9 : 1 and white on Coral 3.2 : 1 are large-text only, so Denim bands carry headlines, not paragraphs, and Coral buttons need bold 14 pt or larger labels. Charcoal on Butter is 5.4 : 1 (AA) and Charcoal on Sage Tint is 7.6 : 1 (AAA). With one text color for everything, the rule is simple: words are Charcoal, color is for fields, marks and the single action button.

Pairings that work

Denim field, white typeHeaders, footers, hero bands. Large text only; body copy goes on a tint instead.
Denim Tint, Charcoal typeThe default card and section combination.
Coral button, white labelOne per screen. Bold, 14 pt minimum.
Butter badge, Charcoal type"New patients welcome", star ratings, small callouts.
Coral Tint, Charcoal typePre-op reminders and anything a parent must not miss.
Sage Tint, Charcoal typeConfirmations, "what's normal after surgery", success messages. Never beside a Coral Tint panel; the pair reads as go/stop.
05 · Typography

Geometric, rounded, readable

The wordmark is set in a geometric sans with round bowls. The brand typefaces echo that geometry without copying it, so headlines feel related to the logo and body copy stays easy to read on a phone at midnight.

Headlines · Outfit
Right Size Care
AaBbCcDdEeFfGgHhIiJjKkLlMmNnOoPpQqRrSsTtUuVvWwXxYyZz 0123456789

Weights 500–600 for headings, 400 for large display quotes. Letter-spacing −1% above 32 px. Free on Google Fonts; fallback Avenir Next, Century Gothic.

Body · Nunito
Gentle on the eyes
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Ear tubes, tonsils, adenoids, sleep apnea, hearing and speech. 0123456789

Regular 400 for paragraphs, Semibold 600 for labels and emphasis, Bold 700 for buttons. Line height 1.6 for reading, 1.4 for UI. Free on Google Fonts; fallback Avenir, system sans.

Type scale

Display · 56Kids only.
H1 · 40Pediatric ENT care in Tampa Bay
H2 · 28What to expect at your first visit
H3 · 20Before the appointment
Body · 17Bring your insurance card, a list of current medications, and any hearing test results from your pediatrician.
Small · 14Office hours vary by location. Same-week appointments are usually available.
Label · 12New patients welcome

The wordmark is part of the logo artwork. Never retype it in Outfit or any other face; always place the logo file.

Setting rules

  • Headlines in sentence case. Reserve all-caps for 12 px labels with 10% tracking.
  • Body copy 60–70 characters per line; never justify.
  • Everything is Charcoal: headlines, body and captions. Hierarchy comes from size and weight, not color.
  • Emphasis is Semibold, not italics or color. Links are Charcoal, underlined; on hover they turn Denim.
  • Numbers in tables and prices use tabular figures.
  • Print collateral uses the same two families; no serif substitutions.
06 · Graphic language & photography

Round, flat, friendly

The animals are flat silhouettes with soft curves. Every other graphic element follows the same rule: rounded corners, flat fills, no outlines, no gradients, no shadows heavier than a card lift.

Shapes and fields

  • Corner radius: 12 px on buttons and inputs, 16 px on cards, 24 px on hero fields. Pills for tags.
  • Build sections from tint fields, not rules or dividers. A page should feel like soft blocks, not a grid of lines.
  • Decorative dots and blobs in the three tints are allowed as background texture at low density. Never over text.
  • Shadows: one soft card lift only (0 8 24 at 12% Charcoal). No inner shadows, bevels or glows.

Icons

Line icons, 2 px stroke, rounded caps and joins, on a 24 px grid, in Charcoal or Denim. Keep the animals as the only filled shapes; everything else is outline so the three friends stay the stars.

Photography

Real families, real offices

Photograph actual patients (with consent), staff and exam rooms. Stock imagery of generic children undermines the trust the brand is built on.

Warm, natural light

Daylight or soft window light, slightly warm white balance. No clinical blue casts, no harsh flash, no heavy filters.

Calm moments

A doctor at a child's eye level, a parent and child reading in the waiting room. Avoid staged smiles at the camera and avoid instruments pointed at kids.

When type sits on a photo, place it over a 60% Charcoal overlay or in a solid tint panel beside the image. Never set white type directly on an unprotected photo.

07 · Voice & tone

Say it the way a good doctor would

We talk to parents the way the best pediatric specialists do in the exam room: plainly, warmly, and without talking down. Tone flexes with the moment; the voice never does.

Clear before clever

Name the condition, say what happens next, say what it means for the child. Wordplay is fine in social posts; never in clinical content.

Calm, not casual

Short sentences. Confident verbs. No exclamation points in anything a worried parent might read at 2 a.m.

Parents are the reader, kids are the subject

Write to the adult, about the child, in a way the child could overhear and feel safe.

Specific and local

Name the office, the doctor, the day. "Our Clearwater office" beats "our conveniently located facilities".

In practice

Ear tubes are a 15-minute procedure. Most kids are back to normal play the next day.
Tympanostomy tube placement is a minimally invasive outpatient surgical intervention with rapid recovery.
We only see children, so everything from the chairs to the instruments is sized for them.
We offer a comprehensive suite of pediatric otolaryngology services.
Same-week appointments are usually available. Call the office nearest you.
Don't wait!! Book NOW and get seen FAST!!
Insist on the Right Size Care.
Insist on the right-sized care experience.

The tagline is always written exactly as Insist on the Right Size Care: title case, no hyphen, no trailing period in display use.
